facts.statement: The study tested whether a saline solution containing hydrogen could treat depression-like symptoms caused by inflammation in mice.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Mice were injected with 0.83 mg/kg of lipopolysaccharide to trigger an inflammatory response.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Thirty minutes after the inflammation trigger, the mice were injected with 5 mL/kg of hydrogen-rich saline.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The treatment reduced signs of anxiety and depression in the mice that had been given the inflammatory agent.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Behavioral changes were measured using open field, elevated plus maze, forced swim, and tail suspension tests.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Blood levels of the inflammatory markers interleukin-1β and tumor necrosis factor-α were lowered by the treatment.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The number of activated microglia cells in the brain was reduced.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The treatment inhibited the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway in the brain.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Synaptic damage in the hippocampus was repaired following the treatment.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The results suggest that giving the hydrogen-rich saline early may reduce inflammation-related depression-like behaviors.
facts.subject: animals
